title: AuroraCloud - Marketplace integration & reference arch sync
summary: Technical sync to align Redwood and AuroraCloud on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture artifacts (VPC, private deployment options, helm/AMI), and next steps for joint solution collateral and testing. Discussed SSO/KMS/audit logs, billing flow, and certification steps for marketplace. Agreed on doc handoffs and a bench test in Redwood sandbox next week.
action_items: Lena Park: Share Redwood marketplace checklist + sample listing draft by 2026-04-02
Mei Lin: Provide AuroraCloud network diagrams + required AMI config by 2026-04-06
Jordan Miles: Stand up Redwood sandbox instance for AuroraCloud integration tests and invite Aurora engineers by 2026-04-08
Carlos Ruiz: Confirm billing & metering requirements for Aurora marketplace (metering dimensions) by 2026-04-03
next_steps: Redwood to email marketplace checklist and GTM PRD template
Schedule joint engineer bench test (45-60m) week of Apr 6
Exchange reference-arch markdown + diagrams in shared drive
Aurora to review security docs (SOC2 summary, KMS options) and list any gaps
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Jordan Miles (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (AuroraCloud PM), Carlos Ruiz (AuroraCloud Marketplace PM), Mei Lin (AuroraCloud Solutions Architect), Tom Becker (AuroraCloud Sec)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros - I'm Lena, I'm the AE on this partnership. Jordan and Samir are our SEs who will lead the technical bits.
[00:15] Priya Sharma: Hi all, Priya here, product. Carlos and Mei will handle the marketplace and infra details.
[00:23] Jordan Miles: Hi, Jordan. Quick agenda: marketplace listing checklist, reference architecture options (hosted vs private), billing/measuring, and then next steps.
[00:35] Carlos Ruiz: Sounds good, we mainly want to understand what's required to list Redwood on Aurora's marketplace and what the joint reference arch looks like for customers who want a private deployment or VPC-connected option.
[00:50] Jordan Miles: Great. I'll start with the listing requirements — high level first. For Aurora marketplace we typically need a short description, support SLA, pricing model (metered dimensions), and a reference arch doc. On Redwood's side, we also need the image/AMI and helm chart for private installs, plus a lightweight SaaS integration spec if you want hosted listing.
[01:10] Mei Lin: When you say AMI and helm chart, is that for on-prem customers or for us to offer a one-click deploy from the marketplace?
[01:20] Jordan Miles: Both. For marketplace one-click provisioning we provide an AMI + terraform scripts for cloud images, and a helm chart for k8s-based installs. There's often small differences in networking assumptions — e.g., whether KV "cash" actually KV cache — can be optional to reduce egress.
[01:35] Priya Sharma: We also need to check compliance — auditors will ask about encryption-at-rest, KMS, SOC2 evidence. Tom, quick note?
[01:45] Tom Becker: Yeah, we'll need SOC2 summary, key rotation policy, and how Redwood handles KMS/HSM integration. Also audit logs for admin actions, retention windows. Can you share a sample audit log format?
[02:00] Lena Park: Absolutely. We'll include SOC2 summary and our KMS integration patterns. We have a standard audit log sample (JSON lines) — we'll attach that in the follow-up.
[02:10] Carlos Ruiz: On billing, we need the metering dims — is Redwood providing per-token metering, instance-hour, or a hybrid?
[02:20] Samir Patel: Currently we support per-token for hosted API, and instance-hour + throughput buckets for dedicated/reserved. For marketplace, many partners want a standardized meter: instance-hour + optional extra for token overages. We can support a mapping table.
[02:35] Priya Sharma: Can Redwood emit usage logs in a format Aurora can ingest? CSV/API?
[02:42] Jordan Miles: Yes, we can provide daily usage exports via S3 or push to your billing endpoint. Provisioning of metering dimensions will be in the marketplace checklist doc.
[02:50] Mei Lin: Network wise, for VPC peering, what connectivity patterns do you recommend? Do you support private link or do we need a NAT?
[03:05] Jordan Miles: We support both. For private deployments we have on-prem install that connects to a private control plane or a fully air-gapped option. For VPC-connected SaaS, PrivateLink or VPC Peering are both supported; we typically recommend PrivateLink for orgs wanting minimal route table changes. Also mention — our KV "cash" actually KV cache — can be optional to reduce egress.
[03:25] Carlos Ruiz: Got it. For the listing, Aurora requires a reference architecture diagram in Visio/PNG and a short runbook — how deep should the runbook be?
[03:35] Lena Park: The runbook should include install steps, basic troubleshooting, upgrade path, and rollback steps for a canary. We can provide a template runbook and a sample diagram.
[03:45] Priya Sharma: On joint solutions — we want a short PRD that describes target customers, value props, and a GTM playbook. Who drafts that?
[03:55] Lena Park: We can draft the first pass of the PRD and GTM, then iterate with you. We'll include suggested collateral and a co-marketing timeline.
[04:05] Mei Lin: A couple technical clarifications: 1) Do you support SAML SSO for admin UI? 2) For KMS, can keys be customer-managed?
[04:15] Samir Patel: Yes on SAML SSO, and yes we support CMKs via KMS integration for Hosted and Dedicated — for Private, customers can provide HSM integration. We'll note the exact flows in the security doc.
[04:25] Tom Becker: Will Redwood provide pen test reports or just SOC2?
[04:30] Jordan Miles: We can share a redacted pen test summary on request plus SOC2 attestation. For marketplace listing, a SOC2 summary is usually enough; some customers will request additional artifacts during procurement.
[04:40] Carlos Ruiz: About one-click provisioning: do you handle AMI updates and auto-updates?
[04:48] Samir Patel: We publish new AMI versions and a semver-like tagged helm chart. The marketplace listing can point to a 'latest' AMI or to a versioned AMI. Auto-update is opt-in; we recommend a canary approach with rollback.
[05:00] Lena Park: Quick call-out — compatibility matrix: we'll include supported k8s versions, supported instance types (GPU/non-GPU), and our recommended quantization/throughput profiles for different workloads.
[05:10] Mei Lin: Perfect. For GPU support we need to know driver requirements and whether CUDA/toolkit needs to be preinstalled.
[05:20] Jordan Miles: We'll share driver docs. For dedicated GPU we supply a container image that assumes the host has NVIDIA drivers and nvidia-container-runtime installed; we have guidance for AMI baking too.
[05:32] Priya Sharma: Any blockers from Redwood side for Aurora's certification?
[05:38] Lena Park: No blockers — just docs and artifacts. One ask: during the initial listing we like to run a small benchmark on your marketplace account to validate perf numbers on a sample workload. That helps the listing page show accurate latency/cost.
[05:50] Carlos Ruiz: That's fine. We'll provision a test account. Timeline?
[05:55] Lena Park: If we can get network diagrams and a sample account by Apr 6, Jordan can spin up a sandbox and run bench tests the week of Apr 6-10.
[06:05] Mei Lin: Do you need anything specific in terms of test prompts or datasets?
[06:12] Jordan Miles: A few representative prompts and expected latencies, ideally a small eval set and token distribution. We can re-run with your dataset to get a realistic cost estimate.
[06:22] Priya Sharma: About support coverage — Aurora requires 24x7 for marketplace launches. What are Redwood's options?
[06:30] Lena Park: We offer tiered support: standard (business hours), premium (24x7), and enterprise (dedicated SE + on-call). For marketplace partners we often recommend premium for the first 90 days. We'll include support SLAs in the checklist.
[06:45] Carlos Ruiz: One more: logos and marketing assets — format/size?
[06:50] Lena Park: We'll send a pack: SVG and PNG, plus a short boilerplate. We'll include legal contacts for co-marketing approvals.
[07:00] Tom Becker: On data residency — if a customer requires EU-only data, how does Redwood handle that for hosted offerings?
[07:10] Samir Patel: We have region pins in our hosted API; we can pin workloads to EU regions and enforce data residency. For guaranteed residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.
[07:22] Mei Lin: Ok great. Any major known limitations we should call out to customers?
[07:30] Jordan Miles: Biggest tradeoffs are latency vs cost on large seq lengths, and for extremely low-latency requirements you may want a dedicated capacity. We'll provide guidance in the recommendations doc.
[07:40] Priya Sharma: That should be fine. Let's outline the concrete deliverables.
[07:45] Lena Park: Deliverables: 1) Redwood sends marketplace checklist and sample listing draft (Lena). 2) Aurora sends network diagrams and AMI requirements (Mei). 3) Redwood stands up sandbox, run bench tests (Jordan). 4) Both collaborate on PRD and GTM timeline (Lena/Priya).
[08:05] Carlos Ruiz: Timeline acceptable. We'll aim to have our internal approvals early next week and get artifacts to you.
[08:15] Jordan Miles: Quick technical note: when we send the reference arch we'll include a minimal helm chart snippet for RBAC and ingress so your operations team can validate.
[08:25] Tom Becker: We'll need to review RBAC, least-privilege.
[08:30] Samir Patel: We'll surface the specific permissions in the runbook.
[08:36] Priya Sharma: Any other risks?
[08:40] Lena Park: The usual: certification could be delayed if security artifacts take time, and billing alignment needs confirmation. But nothing we haven't done before.
[08:50] Carlos Ruiz: Great. If we can get the checklist today, we can start the internal cycle.
[08:55] Lena Park: I'll email the checklist after the call.
[09:00] Mei Lin: Thanks, that'll help.
[09:05] Jordan Miles: We'll plan the bench test for week of Apr 6 and send calendar invites.
[09:12] Lena Park: Ok, let's do a quick recap of next steps then.
[09:18] Priya Sharma: Recap ok for me.
[09:20] Carlos Ruiz: Sounds good.
[09:30] Lena Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and invite.

[47:50] Meeting end.

Notes/links referenced in call:
- Redwood marketplace checklist (to be sent after call) - sample link: https://redwood.ai/marketplace/checklist (placeholder)
- Reference arch template and runbook (Redwood will attach diagrams)
- Benchmark template (token distribution + sample prompts)

Caveats: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings (KV "cash" instead of KV cache, some proper nouns may be off).
